blocks.tagline: A practical guide to the market, the rules of entry and the decisions that matter before committing capital.

paragraphs: First, I want to congratulate you on deciding to become an entrepreneur. It is a choice that can change your life, help you build financial independence and, most importantly, give you something even more valuable: the freedom to decide how you spend your time.
I made that decision many years ago. Looking back, a trusted guide could have helped me avoid mistakes, unnecessary risks and partnerships that did not turn out as I hoped.
Over the years, I have shared these experiences with my family and friends. Yet I have always felt that this knowledge should be accessible to everyone. That is why I created beeside.

I believe every entrepreneur deserves a trusted space to collaborate, find answers, meet the right people and discover opportunities to grow with greater clarity and less friction. That is what we are building, and I genuinely hope it helps you.
In this Doing Business guide, you will find practical information to better understand the market you are exploring and make more informed decisions.
I wish you every success in this new chapter.

blocks.title: Mexico at a glance
blocks.dek: A fast read on market scale, economic conditions and the decisions that need deeper validation.

blocks.label: THE STRATEGIC PICTURE
paragraphs: Mexico combines a large domestic market with established North American production and trade links. Entry potential is real, but national averages hide differences in location, labor availability, infrastructure and regulatory exposure. The most effective entry route depends on the business model, product classification and the need for a local operating entity.

columns.label: OPPORTUNITY SIGNALS
columns.text: Domestic demand and distribution; cross-border supply chains; existing foreign-investor networks; multiple regional operating clusters.

columns.label: WATCH POINTS
columns.text: USMCA review remains open; compliance obligations vary by activity; staffing and infrastructure constraints differ by location; costs cannot be inferred from a national average.

blocks.label: WHAT CHANGED IN 2026
blocks.text: USMCA was not renewed in its existing form at the July review but remains in force; the United States opened public consultation for a 2027 review. Mexico also began a statutory transition toward a 40-hour workweek by 2030.

blocks.title: What must be in place before launch?
blocks.dek: The goal is to map the critical dependencies, not reproduce a directory of every permit.

blocks.label: THE KEY INSIGHT
blocks.text: A company can be legally incorporated and still be unable to invoice, import, employ staff or begin a regulated activity. Operational readiness requires checking what must exist at each point in the transaction and delivery chain.

blocks.title: Minimum national readiness checks
rows: Entity powers, sector restrictions and foreign investment registration
RFC, digital signature, electronic invoices and fiscal duties
Employer registration, social insurance and labor compliance
Importer responsibilities, HS codes, customs and digital trade filings
Marks, licenses and ownership of IP

blocks.text: Sector permits and municipal requirements vary with the activity and site. They should be addressed through a dedicated Knowledge Base query and the project-specific Precision assessment, not an exhaustive national checklist.

blocks.title: Your journey with beeside
blocks.dek: From the first exploration of an opportunity to structured requirements, collaborators and coordinated work.

steps.title: Discovery / Your Expansion View
steps.text: Describe the opportunity or challenge. The initial assessment produces Your Expansion View, an early perspective on the project.

steps.title: Premium + Precision / Understanding
steps.text: Deepen the understanding of your situation and objectives. This phase produces My Service Map.

steps.title: Precision by Category
steps.text: Develop category-specific requirements, leading to Category Requirement Packs (CRP) that help frame the capabilities needed.

steps.title: The Hive + Strategic Advisory
steps.text: Explore specialized partners and, when appropriate, strategic advisory support aligned with the project's needs.

steps.title: Operation Hub + Sherpas
steps.text: Bring people, documents, tasks, deliverables and follow-up into a coordinated collaborative environment.

blocks.text: Your plan, partners and deliverables will be defined by your project. Discovery is the starting point, not a guarantee of an investment outcome or third-party service.
